title: Precision of Welfare-versus-Budget Curves from Unlinked Outcome and Rare-Cost Panels
banked_reason: D0.5 below field floor: incremental, paper_score_ceiling 5.1 < 7.4; independent boundary audit confirms no bounded repair. Math referee passed, but overall panel verdict remains revise with three unrepaired positioning/bibliography findings.
gap_reasons: The delivered results are a whole-class numerical risk bracket, a sharp two-cell comparison, and exact growing-alphabet consistency under n+m ≥ d log(ed)^5. The bracket leaves materially different precision possibilities, while the consistency improvement does not settle sparse shared-design sequences or the general necessary and sufficient oracle follow-up order. Relative to established [polynomial-functional estimation methods](https://arxiv.org/html/1705.00807v7), the delivered advance is a specialized extension to unlinked rare-cost panels; the elementary fixed-alphabet result and abundant-design consistency theorem support subfield rather than field significance. The TL;DR and project justification accurately disclose these boundaries, so there is no stale assertion that the open sharp frontier has been established.

The positioning omits the closest accepted-bank result, stat_discrete_budgetvalue_curve_v1, which already proves a matched whole interior budget-value-curve frontier; state the exact split-panel/rare-unknown-cost theorem-level delta and why the present loose-bracket and consistency deliverables are not subsumed.

The claimed strict improvement is not compared after the theorem with the closest accepted curve result or a closest public result, so the reader cannot assess what is new about this two-panel rare-cost upper/bracket theorem rather than its method labels.

Related work lacks relevance/comparison sentences for listed bibliography items FangSantos2019Directional, Song2014LocalMinimax, PonomarevSemenova2025LowerBand, and LiuLiuSasakiWan2025UniformValues; position each against the delivered consistency/oracle-order result or remove it from the cited list.
proof_attempt_summary: Two D0 solve rounds derived original-record finite risk brackets, a sharp two-cell comparison, and exact consistency under abundant pooled design. The binomial/Bernstein construction does not close the sharp growing-alphabet precision gap or the general necessary-and-sufficient supplied-cost follow-up order; a new localized estimator and matching complete-likelihood converse remain open. The math referee passed, but D0.5 overall remained revise with three unrepaired positioning/bibliography findings, and its achieved incremental tier did not meet the field floor; no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: The target is the population-optimal causal welfare-versus-budget curve from independent, unlinked outcome and cost panels with arbitrary finite covariate masses, unknown propensities, and rare binary treatment costs. Complete-record lower bounds and total finite upper procedures give an explicit, possibly loose precision bracket. A new design-assisted binomial-polynomial procedure improves the plug-in endpoint with abundant auxiliary design records and closes consistency in that resource regime. Capacity-active cost and separate outcome witnesses isolate the two mark shortages. A single anisotropic polynomial price process and complete-record testing are proposed as the construction handle for the still-open sharp all-resource frontier and general oracle-follow-up boundary.
gap: Uncertain-cost allocation identifies priority rules, while discrete nonsmooth-functional estimation analyzes different observation clocks. Neither inspected theorem evaluates original two-panel optimal-curve precision with unknown shared design and rare cost marks.
fill: The research target is an evaluated all-resource risk pair, finite continuous-curve procedures, full-experiment converses, and explicit consistency and oracle-follow-up conditions. The same-polynomial calibration is the central open mathematical content.
